brief: Raymond James's daily note leads with Tech-sector dispersion. AI-slowdown calls from leading firms weighed on stocks, but not uniformly: the S&P 500 Software Index rallied 3.2% while the Semiconductor Index fell 4.4%, which RJ reads as investors differentiating AI infrastructure from software on growth and risk profiles. RJ stays constructive on Tech overall despite expected near-term leadership rotation. Separately, RJ flags the Russell 2000 as 3Q26's weakest major US index because smaller companies are more rate-sensitive, closing below the 2,910 support/resistance level for a third day with 2,800 as next support. RJ continues to favor large caps for their diversified revenue, stronger balance sheets and lower cost of capital. A fourth straight day of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline outage (Houthi attacks amid the US-Iran conflict, cutting about 4 million barrels a day) is keeping WTI near $102, which in turn pushed the 10-year yield to a 5.02% intraday high, matching 2007, before it closed at 4.99%. RJ still expects yields lower long-term but says a sustained decline needs oil to ease first. A Lehman-anniversary sidebar notes the S&P 500 has since gained 537%.
